why: The record of every hand edit to the DELE Spanish decks. Applied by spanish-fix.js; see that file's header for what an entry may carry and why the record exists at all. DELE A1 WAS READ IN FULL in Sep 2026, one card at a time in batches of ten - all 493 of them - and this is what that pass changed: 486 cards carry a correction and 8 were read and left alone. The counts in the deck's own description (220 nouns with their article, 63 feminine pairs) are the GENERATOR's and were deliberately not recomputed: they use categories run.py knows and this record cannot reproduce, and a figure quietly rewritten to a different rule is worse than one left as it was. The word count IS maintained, through the descSub chain.

delea1.why: Folding the eight article cards into two and adding the three third-person object pronouns the generator's word list has no entry for changes what the deck holds, and a subtitle that goes on counting the old number is a claim the file itself refutes. The count was already wrong before any of this - the subtitle said 500 against 496 cards - so both figures are set to what is actually there. Both the 500 and the 490 pair are kept, so the chain still works on a deck freshly rebuilt from the generator. The figure was 493 for one commit, written when the plan was three inserted pronouns and left when it turned out to be two: les is a form on the le card rather than a card. A count in prose is wrong the moment the thing it counts moves, which is why check-claims.js exists one directory over — check it against the file rather than against the intention. It moved again when la tercera turned out to be a duplicate of tercero, tercera and was folded away: every count in the chain is kept so it still works on a deck freshly rebuilt from the generator. It moved once more when the DEFINITE and INDEFINITE article cards were folded together into one: 493 to 492. Every figure in the chain is kept, so the record still works on a deck freshly rebuilt from the generator. NAME TABLE WIDENED (Sep 2026, DELE A2 batch S2): Tatoeba's Spanish side often renders Mary and John as María and Juan, so a table renaming only the English names split a sentence in two - 'Quizá Carlos no quiere que encontremos a María' over 'Maybe Carlos doesn't want us to find Ana'. María, Maria, Marie and Juan are now renamed on both sides.

caña.desc: A small glass of draught beer, and what is ordered in a bar in Spain far more often than una cerveza. It is roughly a third of a pint, served cold and often with a free tapa beside it in some regions.

tapa.desc: A small plate of food served with a drink. In Granada, León and parts of Andalusia it comes free with the drink; almost everywhere else it is ordered and paid for.

instituto.desc: The state secondary school in Spain, which pupils enter at about twelve. It is not el colegio, which is the primary school or a private school covering both stages, and not the English word institute.

DNI.desc: El Documento Nacional de Identidad, the Spanish identity card, carried by every resident and asked for at a bank, a hotel desk and an exam. A foreigner's equivalent is the NIE.

mercadillo.desc: An open-air street market held on a fixed day of the week, selling clothes, household goods and produce from stalls. It is the small weekly sort, as against el mercado, the permanent covered market hall.

piso.desc: A flat, and the ordinary word for a home in a Spanish town, where most people live in one rather than in a house. It also means a storey, so el tercer piso is both the third floor and a flat on it.

paella.desc: A rice dish cooked flat in a wide shallow pan, from Valencia, where the traditional one is made with rabbit, chicken and beans rather than seafood. The pan gives the dish its name.

siesta.desc: The rest taken after the midday meal, in practice more often a closed shop than a sleep. Many small businesses in Spain still shut between about two and five and open again into the evening.

tortilla.desc: In Spain, a thick omelette of egg, potato and onion, served in wedges hot or cold and eaten at any hour. In Mexico the same word is a flat maize or wheat bread, which is a different food entirely.

usted.desc: The polite form of address, taking third-person verbs. In Spain it is now reserved for strangers much older than the speaker and for formal dealings; across most of Latin America it is used far more widely.

vosotros.desc: The plural you used when speaking to more than one person addressed as tú. It is Spain only: Latin America uses ustedes to any group, formal or not, and a learner there will never need the form.

euro.desc: The currency of Spain since 2002, divided into a hundred céntimos. Prices are written with a comma for the decimal point and the symbol after the figure: 3,50 €.

Semana Santa.desc: The week before Easter, and the largest religious festival of the Spanish year, marked by processions in most towns and by a national holiday from Thursday to Sunday. Schools and many businesses close for the whole week.

Nochevieja.desc: New Year's Eve, on which it is the custom to eat twelve grapes, one at each chime of midnight. Nochebuena, the night before it in the calendar's other sense, is Christmas Eve.

carné.desc: A card that licenses or identifies: el carné de conducir is the driving licence, el carné de identidad the identity card, el carné joven the youth discount card. Also spelt carnet.

delea1/de.why: The third bullet - 'used after the thing owned and before the owner' - was a usage NOTE standing in the list of translations, where the card renders it as though it were an English equivalent of the word. It moves into the gloss it qualifies. The list also left out three senses an A1 reader meets in the first week: origin (soy de Madrid), material (de madera) and topic (un libro de historia). Examples 2 and 3 were the same sentence with its two halves swapped - 'La esencia de las matematicas es la libertad' and 'La esencia de la libertad son las matematicas' - so the card showed one example twice; the second is dropped for a sentence that shows the origin sense.
senses: 's (after the thing owned, before the owner)
dropEx: La esencia de la libertad son las matemáticas.
ex: ¿De dónde eres?
Where are you from?

delea1/que.why: Glossed as a conjunction only, so the RELATIVE PRONOUN - which is what its own first example shows, and one of the two commonest uses of the commonest word in Spanish - was missing. That example made the loss invisible: 'El color que me encanta es el rojo' was translated 'My favorite color is red', which translates the que away, so the card asked a reader to learn a word from a sentence whose English does not contain it. It is dropped for a sentence whose translation carries the relative through. DEDUPLICATION PASS (Sep 2026, on request). 181 example sentences were serving two or more cards each — 424 of the deck's 1,477 slots — because the corpus a function word draws from is small and one sentence legitimately contains de, que and antes at once. A reader working through the deck in order met the same sentence up to three times as though it were new. The sentence is KEPT on the commonest of the words that share it, by the deck's own frequency order, and authored afresh on the rest.
dropEx: El color que me encanta es el rojo.
No abrir antes de que pare el tren.
ex: Este es el libro que me gusta.
This is the book that I like.
Este es el libro que te dije.

delea1/no.why: Glossed 'not' alone. The commonest English translation of Spanish no - no, in answer to a question - was missing, and the deck carries si as 'yes, yeah', so the pair was taught from one side only. The third example, 'No abrir antes de que pare el tren', is one of the deck's most reused sentences (it also illustrates de and que) and is an infinitive notice rather than everyday speech; it makes room for an answer.
dropEx: No abrir antes de que pare el tren.
ex: —¿Quieres café? —No, gracias.
"Do you want coffee?" "No, thanks."

delea1/la.why: THE ARTICLES, FOLDED INTO ONE CARD WITH A TABLE (Sep 2026, on request: "in the Spanish decks, fold the articles into one card, with a conjugation table"). THE DEFINITE ARTICLE, FOLDED FROM FOUR CARDS INTO ONE. el, la, los and las were four separate notes for one paradigm, which the deck's own stated policy already refuses everywhere else - a noun's plural sits beneath it and a feminine pair is taught as one card (el nino, la nina above los ninos, las ninas, 63 of them). Split, the four glosses had drifted apart: los was filed as a PRONOUN ('plural masculine or neuter pronoun') with 'the' missing altogether, though all three of its own examples used it as an article. Split, they also collided on the reverse card, where three of them prompted the reader with 'the' and nothing else. The surviving note keeps the lowest id of the four (u_delea1_4), which is the earliest and most frequent slot. The paradigm moves into Forms, where a paradigm belongs, and takes the el agua rule with it - which the deck was already illustrating on this card, in the example about oil and water, without saying anywhere what the reader was looking at. The third example, 'con los que charlar', uses los as a relative rather than as an article; it is dropped for one that shows the masculine plural plainly. AND ITS EXAMPLES ARE GRADED AT THE HEAD OF THE DECK: measured over the first forty cards every example ran to eight words or more here, where the deck's median is ten and a reader on their first day should meet something shorter. One short sentence replaces the longest. THE INDEFINITE ARTICLE NOW JOINS IT, on the same reasoning one level up: el/la/los/las and un/una/unos/unas are one system with one shape - two genders, two numbers - and a learner who knows that shape knows both halves of it. Taught apart, the reader met the same grid twice and was never shown that it IS the same grid. AND THE PARADIGM MOVES OUT OF Forms INTO A TABLE: eight forms in two genders and two numbers is a grid, and `uc-forms` is a list of label-and-value pairs, which is why the definite article's three rows read as three unrelated notes rather than as one paradigm. It uses the card type's own conjugation markup, so it looks like every other table in the deck. The numeral uno keeps its own card, and so do lo, la, le and les, which are pronouns rather than articles. FIVE EXAMPLES, AND THE RECORD SAYS WHY: the deck gives every card three, and this one now teaches eight forms in two paradigms - three sentences cannot show both articles in both genders and both numbers, and a card whose whole point is the shape of a grid should not illustrate a quarter of it. The generator's own el agua sentence is kept as the first, since it is the one that shows the stressed-a rule the Forms row states.
senses: unos, unas before a number — about, approximately
forms: el agua, las aguas — but una/alguna agua

Worse, none of the three examples taught the word: the first is the proverb 'No hay mal que por bien no venga', where bien is a NOUN; the second bolded bienes, the plural of that noun meaning goods; and the third bolded Mejor, which is bien's comparative and is the word that sentence actually teaches. The comparative has no card of its own, so it goes in Forms, and the three examples are replaced with the adverb.

Replaced, and the gloss now says what neuter means here: eso points at an idea or a situation rather than at a noun.

The headword becomes vale, the interjection first, and the noun keeps its sense and its plural beneath it.

Each pupil has a computer.

delea2/cierto, cierta.why: 'true' alone, where the word has a second sense before a noun — cierta gente, 'certain people' — and a phrase, por cierto, 'by the way', that an A2 reader uses constantly. All three examples were ser cierto, one construction three times, so two go.

delea2/quien.why: The gloss named neither the plural quienes, which the second example shows, nor the 'whoever' sense of the third. 'Your father wants you' dropped the whole point of 'Es a ti a quien quiere tu padre', which is the emphasis; the Spanish name Ana is now matched in the English, which had Ann.

delea2/pasado, pasada.why: THE THIRD EXAMPLE WAS NOT SPANISH: 'el fin de semana pasada' makes the adjective agree with semana rather than with fin de semana, which is masculine. What did you do last weekend?

I don't want to talk about the past.

My head hurts.

delea2/mientras.why: Glossed 'meanwhile' as an adverb, which is mientras tanto; on its own mientras is the conjunction 'while', and that is what all three examples show. The third wrote 'un Señor' with a capital, which Spanish does not use for señor before a name.
dropEx: mientras tú no estabas
ex: Mientras tanto, yo preparo la cena.
Meanwhile, I'll make dinner.

delea2/pues.why: The gloss led with 'so, then, in that case, because, since' and never gave 'well', which is what pues most often means in speech and what two of the three examples show — the second an idiom, estar como una cabra. The idiom goes, for the 'then' sense; and the third example's translation had the tense wrong.
senses: well (at the start of a reply: pues no sé)
dropEx: Pues sí que estás como una cabra.

delea2/contra.why: Two of the three examples were estar en contra de, the same construction twice, and the physical sense — against a wall, into a tree — was not shown. 'versus' is a real use (España contra Francia) and is kept.

dropEx: totalmente en contra de la pena capital

The car crashed into a tree.

delea2/la persona.why: The gloss was a definition split into bullets in the wrong place — 'person (an individual', 'usually a human being)' — plus a second sense the Spanish word does not have. What the card did need to say is that la persona is feminine whatever the person, which the first example (él es una persona) shows without saying. Two translations were off: the definite article in 'The people don't like the birds' is Spanish grammar rather than English, and 'the happiest man on earth' for 'la persona más feliz del mundo'.
forms: always feminine, even of a man: él es una buena persona
exEn: A las personas no les gustan los pájaros.
People don't like birds.
Yo era la persona más feliz del mundo.
I was the happiest person in the world.

delea2/dentro.why: The gloss gave only the place sense, where one of the three examples was dentro de for time — 'in an hour' — which is how an A2 reader meets it most. 'no dentro de mucho' is a calque of 'before long' rather than Spanish. The third example is also an A1 sentence. senses: dentro de — inside (dentro de la caja)

dropEx: no dentro de mucho
cerrada con llave desde dentro

The children are playing inside because it's raining.
El móvil está dentro de mi bolso.
My mobile is in my bag.

delea2/hacia.why: 'toward' and 'towards' are one word spelt two ways, the first American; 'around' and 'about' are the time sense. All three examples were also A1 sentences, so all three are replaced, one per sense. I have a lot of respect for her.

delea2/la suerte.why: 'lot' is a sense only in echar a suertes — to draw lots — which is the second example and is not A2 Spanish. The phrases a reader does need, ¡buena suerte!, tener suerte and por suerte, were not named. The first example is also an A1 sentence. Echémoslo a suertes.

Good luck in the exam!

Luckily, it didn't rain.

delea2/dejar.why: The gloss missed the two uses an A2 reader needs most: 'to let' (mis padres no me dejan salir) and dejar de + infinitive, 'to stop doing', which two of the three examples actually were. All three were also A1 sentences, and the third, 'el agua dada', is not Spanish (it wants abierta). SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

dejó de fumar
el agua dada

Mis padres no me dejan salir por la noche.
My parents don't let me go out at night.
Mi padre dejó de fumar hace años.
My father stopped smoking years ago.

delea2/importante.why: 'that cares' and 'that matters.' are fragments of a dictionary definition, full stop included, standing as translations. The examples are right.

delea2/el miedo.why: Two of the three examples were dar miedo, one construction twice, and both were also A1 sentences; tener miedo, the way a reader says they are afraid, was not shown. My sister is scared of spiders.

delea2/adelante.why: Two of the three examples were de ahora en adelante, and the first was an awkward calque ('dos kilómetros hacia adelante'). ¡Adelante! — 'come in', 'go ahead' — which a reader hears at every door, was nowhere.

Take a step forward.

delea2/encontrarse.why: The gloss gives three senses and all three examples showed one, 'to meet' — and two of them were also A1 sentences. ¿Cómo te encuentras? and se encuentra en, the other two, are both everyday A2 Spanish. dropEx: con Ana en el desayuno
con quien se encontraba

The museum is in the centre.

delea2/la mano.why: 'front foot' is an animal's forefoot and not what an A2 reader needs, while the card said nothing about the one fact that trips everybody: la mano is feminine though it ends in -o. The first example translated a singular as 'hands', and the third is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

dropEx: le está tomando la mano
La niña tomó la mano de su madre.

Me dio la mano.
He shook my hand.

delea2/único, única.why: Five English words for two senses. Two of the three examples were 'the only X', and 'One can but try' is an archaism standing for 'the only thing we can do is try'; the unique sense had no example.

dropEx: Las fotografías son las únicas pruebas
exEn: Lo único que se puede hacer
The only thing we can do is try.

It's a unique opportunity.

delea2/incluso, inclusa.why: THE CARD TAUGHT A WORD NOBODY USES AND ITS EXAMPLES TAUGHT ANOTHER. incluso as an adjective, 'enclosed', is archaic, and inclusa is not its feminine but a noun, an old word for a foundling home; every example is the adverb incluso, 'even', which is the word. The headword loses its false feminine and its plurals, and two examples that were also A1 sentences are replaced. delea2/aunque.why: A dictionary's list — 'albeit', 'irrespective of' — where the card needs the one rule: aunque with the indicative states a fact (although), with the subjunctive a possibility (even if). Two of the examples were the subjunctive; the third, 'Aunque yo te digo, tú no lo haces', is not idiomatic Spanish. So one subjunctive stays and a matched pair is added.
senses: although, even though (+ indicative: aunque llueve)
dropEx: aunque no lo parezca
Aunque yo te digo

Although it's raining, we're going out.
Iré aunque llueva.
I'll go even if it rains.

delea2/arriba.why: 'uphill' and 'upstream' are dictionary senses no A2 reader needs, and all three examples were 'upstairs', one of them an A1 sentence and one carrying an English name and a tense its Spanish does not have. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

dropEx: Mi habitación está en el piso de arriba.

Look up.
Estoy mojado de arriba abajo.
I'm soaked from head to toe.

delea2/la guerra.why: The first and third examples said the same thing — no more wars — and the third wrote sólo, whose accent the Academy dropped in 2010.
dropEx: Si tan sólo no hubiera
ex: Mi abuelo luchó en la guerra.
My grandfather fought in the war.

delea2/igual.why: The gloss was a dictionary definition in four parts, and none of it said me da igual — 'I don't mind' — though that is the third example and among the commonest things said in Spain. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: the same (igual que — the same as)
me da igual — I don't mind, it's all the same to me
al igual que — like, just as
dropEx: Él no es alto, al igual que yo.
ex: Tu bolso es igual que el mío.
Your bag is the same as mine.

delea2/abajo.why: Two examples where the corpus had no third, and the second is an awkward rendering of 'he looked down at his shoes'. It stays, being Spanish, and a third is added.
ex: Vivo dos pisos más abajo.
I live two floors down.

delea2/fuerte.why: 'loud' is in the gloss and in no example; the first two examples were más fuerte que, one construction twice, and the third is also an A1 sentence. The adverb — habla más fuerte — was not named. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: son más fuertes que nosotros
le gusta el café fuerte

The lion is stronger than the wolf.

The music is very loud.
Habla más fuerte, por favor.
Speak louder, please.

delea2/atrás.why: 'hace un rato atrás' says ago twice, a pleonasm the standard language avoids; años atrás is the construction the gloss's 'ago' means. 'back in time' is a definition rather than a translation.
senses: behind (quedarse atrás — to be left behind)
dropEx: hace un rato atrás
ex: Años atrás vivíamos en Toledo.
Years ago we lived in Toledo.

delea2/el/la bebé.why: THE SECOND EXAMPLE WAS SPELT WRONG AND BOLDED THE WRONG WORD: 'su bebe' without its accent is the verb beber, 'drinks', and that is what the card marked. The first example translated papá as 'dada'.
dropEx: Ella cogió a su bebe
exEn: primera palabra de mi bebé
My baby's first word was "Dad".
ex: Ana tuvo un bebé el mes pasado.
Ana had a baby last month.

delea2/mayor.why: The gloss led with 'of age' and 'major' and never said 'older' or 'bigger' — the comparative of grande and viejo, which is what mayor is — nor mi hermano mayor, the phrase an A2 reader needs first. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: el mayor, la mayor — the oldest, the biggest
mayor de edad — adult, of age
dropEx: ¿Cuál es mayor, Japón o el Reino Unido?
ex: Mi hermano mayor vive en Londres.
My older brother lives in London.

delea2/morir.why: The first example is a mistranslated proverb ('those whom the gods love die young' rendered as 'those who love God') and is also an A1 sentence. morirse de, the everyday form behind the second example, was not named. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: morirse de (hambre, risa…) — to be dying of (hunger, laughing…)
dropEx: Las personas que aman a Dios mueren jóvenes.
ex: Mi abuelo murió en 2010.
My grandfather died in 2010.

delea2/la lista.why: TWO OF THE THREE EXAMPLES WERE A DIFFERENT WORD: 'la cena esté lista' and '¿Estáis listas?' are the adjective listo, 'ready', matched on shared letters. 'roll' and 'stripe' are not A2 senses. The coincidence goes in Forms, where a reader will want it.
senses: la lista de la compra — the shopping list
pasar lista — to take the register
forms: lista — feminine of listo, ready: la cena está lista
dropEx: La cena probablemente esté lista
Estáis listas
ex: He hecho la lista de la compra.
I've made the shopping list.
Tengo una lista de cosas que hacer.
I have a list of things to do.

delea2/seguir.why: The gloss had 'to continue' and 'to keep on' with no word on seguir + gerund — sigue lloviendo, 'it's still raining' — which is how the verb is used most. Two of the examples were 'follow someone's advice', and the first is also an A1 sentence; seguir recto, the directions a reader asks for, was missing. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to continue, to go on (seguir + gerund: sigue lloviendo — it's still raining)
seguir (todo) recto — to go straight on
dropEx: seguir los consejos de su maestro
haber seguido el consejo
ex: Sigue lloviendo.
It's still raining.
Siga todo recto.
Go straight on.

delea2/medio, media.why: The second example is the noun medios, 'means', mistranslated as 'proper methods', and the gloss said 'half' twice, the second time with a definition. The third is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: y media — half past (las tres y media)
dropEx: por sus propios medios
La escuela empieza a las ocho y media.
ex: Quiero medio kilo de tomates.
I'd like half a kilo of tomatoes.
Son las tres y media.
It's half past three.

delea2/la seguridad.why: 'Deberías de estas más atento' has a typo for estar, and '¡Llama a Seguridad!' capitalises a common noun mid-sentence. The plural las seguridades is a form nobody uses, so it comes out of Forms.
dropEx: ¡Llama a Seguridad!
Deberías de estas
ex: La seguridad de los niños es lo más importante.
The children's safety is what matters most.
Habla con mucha seguridad.
He speaks with great confidence.

delea2/además.why: Eight English words for one meaning. The first example said María in the Spanish and Ana in the English, and 'ya no ama más' says 'no longer' twice. The second and third were both además de; the third's 'not to mention' reverses the emphasis. The second stays, in British English.
senses: además de — as well as, besides
dropEx: ya no ama más
además de inglés
exEn: Esa tienda vende muchas cosas
That shop sells many things besides furniture.
ex: Es barato y, además, está muy cerca.
It's cheap and, what's more, it's very close.
Además, no tengo tiempo.
Besides, I don't have time.

delea2/el oído.why: TWO OF THE THREE EXAMPLES WERE A DIFFERENT WORD: 'haber oído' and 'puede ser oída' are the past participle of oír, matched on shared letters. That coincidence goes in Forms; the ear and the ear for music get examples.
senses: tener buen oído — to have a good ear
forms: oído — past participle of oír: lo he oído
dropEx: Recuerdo ya haber oído
puede ser oída
ex: Me duele el oído.
I've got earache.
Tiene muy buen oído para la música.
She has a very good ear for music.

delea2/la luz.why: 'lumen' is a unit of measurement, not a translation, and the card never gave la luz for the electricity supply — the bill every flat in Spain pays. Two of the three examples were also A1 sentences, one of them using pieza for 'room', which is Latin American. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: electricity, power (la factura de la luz — the electricity bill)
dropEx: A esta pieza le llega luz del sol.
Había luz de luna ayer por la noche.
ex: Me gusta la luz de esta habitación.
I like the light in this room.
Este mes la factura de la luz es muy alta.
The electricity bill is very high this month.

delea2/conseguir.why: The gloss was one line of five near-synonyms for 'achieve' and never said 'to get' — the commonest sense, and the one its own first example shows — nor conseguir + infinitive, 'to manage to'. The third example is consigo, the pronoun 'with him', matched on shared letters; that coincidence goes in Forms. The second is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to achieve, to manage (conseguir + infinitive — to manage to)
forms: consigo — with him, with her, with oneself (con + sí)
dropEx: Eso es lo que consigues por no escuchar.
no llevaba la dirección
ex: ¿Dónde conseguiste esas entradas?
Where did you get those tickets?
Por fin conseguí aprobar el examen.
I finally managed to pass the exam.

delea2/la paz.why: The gloss was two dictionary definitions in brackets. The examples are good — three different uses — but two of them are phrases the gloss never named: dejar en paz and hacer las paces.
senses: dejar en paz — to leave alone
hacer las paces — to make up (after a quarrel)

delea2/peor.why: 'Está es la peor pesadilla' writes the demonstrative esta with the accent of the verb está. The adverb — me encuentro peor — had no example and no line.
senses: el peor, la peor — the worst
dropEx: la peor pesadilla de todo piloto
ex: Hoy me encuentro peor.
I feel worse today.

delea2/llamar.why: 'to summon' led the gloss, and 'to refer to' stood for llamar in the naming sense; llamar a la puerta, 'to knock', was missing. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to call (by a name: lo llaman Pepe)
to knock, to ring (llamar a la puerta)
dropEx: Seguramente él me llamará por teléfono esta noche.
ex: Alguien está llamando a la puerta.
Someone is knocking at the door.

delea2/ponerse.why: THE GERUND WAS SPELT WRONG: 'poníendose' accents the i of -iendo, where the stress, and so the written accent, falls on the e (poniéndose). The generator's enclitic_gerund matched `ie` and accented its first letter, and missed -yendo altogether; measured over the six decks, 82 reflexive gerunds carry the fault — every -er and -ir one — and it is fixed in build_deck.py. Two examples were also A1 sentences, and ponerse a + infinitive, 'to start', was not named. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to become, to get (ponerse nervioso — to get nervous)
dropEx: El cielo se puso cada vez más oscuro.
rara vez se pone su camisa negra
ex: Me pongo nervioso antes de los exámenes.
I get nervous before exams.
De repente se puso a llover.
Suddenly it started to rain.

delea2/el perro, la perra.why: 'lazy person' is a regional slang sense and not A2; what la perra does mean is a female dog. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: El perro es el mejor amigo del hombre.
ex: Saco al perro todas las mañanas.
I take the dog out every morning.

delea2/el cielo.why: Two of the three examples were heaven, one of them an archaism ('la venganza de los cielos'), and the everyday sky — el cielo está despejado — had none. The helicopter's 'circling above' drops what the Spanish says.
dropEx: La venganza de los cielos
exEn: El helicóptero está dando vueltas
The helicopter is circling in the sky.
ex: Hoy el cielo está despejado.
The sky is clear today.

delea2/el viaje.why: 'voyage' led the gloss; the word is 'trip'. The third example, 'Él piensa en el próximo viaje de ella', is a stilted construction, and ¡buen viaje! was not on the card.
senses: hacer un viaje — to go on a trip
dropEx: Él piensa en el próximo viaje de ella.
ex: ¡Buen viaje!
Have a good trip!

delea2/detrás.why: 'after' is not a sense of detrás, and the adverb on its own — nos sentamos detrás — had no example, all three being detrás de. The second is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: cierra la puerta detrás de ti
ex: Nosotros nos sentamos detrás.
We sat at the back.

delea2/libre.why: Two definitions in brackets, neither the sense a reader needs first — free as in not busy or not taken (¿está libre este asiento?) — and nothing on the false friend: free of charge is gratis, never libre. 'He has no leisure for sport' is an archaism, and 'compras libres de impuestos acá' is awkward Spanish with a Latin American acá.
senses: free (not busy, not taken: tiempo libre, un asiento libre)
forms: free of charge — that is gratis
dropEx: compras libres de impuestos
exEn: no tiene tiempo libre para hacer deportes
He has no free time for sport.
ex: ¿Está libre este asiento?
Is this seat free?

delea2/cual.why: The gloss was cual as an archaic adverb, 'like, in the manner of', which is literary; the word an A2 reader meets is the relative el cual, la cual, lo cual, and ¿cuál?, with its accent, in questions. 'Ellos no tienen ni idea de cuales son nuestros problemas' is that interrogative and is spelt wrong — an indirect question keeps the accent (cuáles) — and 'algo de lo cual podamos hablar' is stilted.
senses: el cual, la cual, lo cual — which, who (after a preposition or a comma)
dropEx: de cuales son nuestros problemas
algo de lo cual podamos hablar
ex: Perdí las llaves, lo cual fue un problema.
I lost my keys, which was a problem.
La casa en la cual nací ya no existe.
The house in which I was born no longer exists.

delea2/el cambio.why: 'shift' is not an A2 sense; the change a shop hands back was only in the gloss and the phrases en cambio and a cambio de were missing. The exchange-rate example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: exchange (el tipo de cambio — the exchange rate)
en cambio — on the other hand
a cambio de — in exchange for
dropEx: ¿Cuál es el tipo de cambio de hoy?
ex: Aquí tiene el cambio.
Here's your change.

delea2/la ropa.why: 'robes' is not a translation, and the card did not say the one thing that trips English speakers: la ropa is singular where English says 'clothes'. Its second example used the rare plural as if it were ordinary; the third is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: lavar la ropa — to do the washing
forms: singular in Spanish where English says 'clothes': toda mi ropa
dropEx: Sus ropas siempre tienen mal olor.
caminando por ahí en ropa interior
ex: Voy a lavar la ropa.
I'm going to do the washing.
Esta tienda vende ropa interior.
This shop sells underwear.

delea2/perder.why: 'to get lost' is perderse, a different card's business; what perder itself lacked was 'to miss' (perder el tren) and 'to waste' (perder el tiempo). All three examples were 'lose', so one gives way to the train.
senses: to miss (perder el tren — to miss the train)
to waste (perder el tiempo — to waste time)
dropEx: El otro día perdí mi cámara de fotos.
ex: Si no te das prisa, vamos a perder el tren.
If you don't hurry, we'll miss the train.

delea2/perfecto, perfecta.why: Right as a card; one translation had the tense wrong, me queda being present.
exEn: me queda perfecta
The shirt you gave me fits me perfectly.

delea2/derecho, derecha.why: THE GLOSS NAMED NEITHER SENSE THE EXAMPLES SHOWED. It gave 'straight, upright', while the first example is 'right' as against left (el guante derecho) and the second is the noun los derechos, 'rights'. The third is la derecha, an A1 card and an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Miró hacia la izquierda y hacia la derecha.
ex: Ponte derecho.
Stand up straight.

delea2/el sexo.why: One example, and a gloss saying the same thing twice in two definitions. The word is on every form an A2 candidate fills in.
senses: sex (male or female — sexo: hombre / mujer, on a form)
ex: Escriba su nombre, su edad y su sexo.
Write your name, age and sex.
Los dos sexos tienen los mismos derechos.
Both sexes have the same rights.

delea2/encima.why: All three examples were por encima de, and two of them were 'above average', one construction and one meaning twice. encima de, 'on top of', and encima meaning 'what's more' were not shown.
senses: on you (¿llevas dinero encima? — have you got any money on you?)
what's more, on top of that (y encima llegó tarde)
encima de — on, on top of
dropEx: por encima de la altura media
ex: Deja el libro encima de la mesa.
Leave the book on the table.

delea2/diferente.why: The first example is also an A1 sentence, and the one S1 took off la vida for the same reason. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Ahora veo la vida de un modo diferente.
ex: Somos muy diferentes.
We're very different.

delea2/cambiarse.why: The first example is the plain verb cambiar — '¿Cuándo cambiaste la foto de tu perfil?' — and 'to move house' is mudarse in Spain, cambiarse de casa being mainly Latin American. AND ITS AFFIRMATIVE IMPERATIVE WAS WRONG, found in batch S6: cambíate, cambíese, cambíense put the accent on the i of the diphthong, where Spanish writes cámbiate, cámbiese, cámbiense (cambio, not cambío).
senses: to change (clothes: cambiarse de ropa), to get changed
cambiarse de casa — to move house (Spain usually says mudarse)
dropEx: ¿Cuándo cambiaste la foto de tu perfil?
ex: Me cambio de ropa y salimos.
I'll get changed and we'll go out.

delea2/el sino.why: THE CARD HAD THE WRONG WORD AT ITS HEAD. el sino, 'fate', is literary; every example is the conjunction sino, 'but (rather)', after a negative — which is the A2 word, the one that has to be told apart from pero. The headword becomes sino, the conjunction first and the literary noun kept beneath it; its plural goes. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: but, but rather (after a negative: no es rojo sino azul)
no solo … sino también — not only … but also
dropEx: Él no hace otra cosa sino leer manga.
ex: No solo habla inglés, sino también francés.
She speaks not only English but also French.

delea2/la boca.why: 'oral cavity' is a definition and 'opening' a gloss of the entrance sense, which had no example — la boca del metro is how a reader meets it. The first example was an idiom glossed with a different idiom.
senses: entrance (la boca del metro — the metro entrance)
dropEx: Se me sale el corazón por la boca.
ex: Nos vemos en la boca del metro.
See you at the metro entrance.

delea2/el error.why: 'error' alone, where the everyday English is 'mistake', and cometer un error, the verb it takes, was not named. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: cometer un error — to make a mistake
dropEx: No voy a permitir tus errores nunca más.
ex: Perdona, ha sido un error.
Sorry, it was a mistake.

delea2/el sueño.why: THE GLOSS AND THE EXAMPLES DISAGREED ENTIRELY: 'sleep, slumber, sleepiness' over three sentences all saying a dream had come true, one construction three times. Both senses belong on the card, and tener sueño — 'to be sleepy' — which is the use an A2 reader needs.
dropEx: Espero que todos tus sueños
Su sueño se ha convertido
ex: Tengo mucho sueño.
I'm very sleepy.
Necesito ocho horas de sueño.
I need eight hours' sleep.

delea2/ambos.why: 'Carlos no puede darse el lujo de ambos' is a calque of 'can't afford both' that no Spanish speaker would say, and the card did not show ambos before a noun, which is its commonest position. Its feminine was in no Forms row.
dropEx: darse el lujo de ambos
ex: Ambos hermanos viven en Madrid.
Both brothers live in Madrid.

delea2/el dolor.why: The gloss ran seven words of one sense together — 'pain, ache, aching soreness, tenderness (physical)' — and only two examples, one of them an A1 sentence. dolor de + body part is the construction an A2 reader needs, and grief has an example now. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Se me ha ido el dolor de cabeza.
ex: Tengo dolor de espalda.
I've got backache.
Sintió un gran dolor cuando murió su padre.
He felt great grief when his father died.

delea2/ganar.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES TAUGHT THE CARD, AND THE GLOSS LEFT OUT 'TO WIN'. Two were the noun las ganas ('me da la gana', 'no tengo ganas de'), matched on shared letters; the third is seguro's sentence, kept there. 'to win' is the commonest sense there is. The noun goes in Forms, and the three senses get an example each. SHARED WITH AN EARLIER A2 CARD, which keeps it.
senses: to gain, to put on (weight: he ganado dos kilos)
forms: las ganas — wish, desire (tener ganas de — to feel like)
dropEx: Estoy seguro de que ellos van a ganar.
lo que me da la gana
no tengo ganas de beber alcohol
ex: España ganó el partido.
Spain won the match.
Mi hermana gana mucho dinero.
My sister earns a lot of money.
He ganado dos kilos.
I've put on two kilos.

delea2/la cita.why: The first and third examples were the same sentence twice — an appointment at half past two — and the romantic date, the gloss's first sense, had none.
senses: pedir cita — to make an appointment
dropEx: Tengo una cita a las dos y media.
ex: Esta noche tengo una cita con Ana.
Tonight I have a date with Ana.

delea2/pobre.why: The gloss had been split into bullets inside its brackets ('lacking money', 'resources', 'etc.)'), and it did not say what decides the sense: pobre after the noun is poor, before it is pitiable. The examples show both and are kept.

delea2/tras.why: A dictionary's list of five, where the card needs to say that tras is the formal 'after' beside después de. 'cierre la puerta tras de usted' is not current Spanish (tras usted), and it and 'tras tres años' are both A1 sentences. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: after (more formal than después de: tras la cena)
día tras día — day after day
dropEx: cierre la puerta tras de usted
tras tres años de ausencia
ex: Tras la cena, salimos a pasear.
After dinner, we went out for a walk.
Día tras día, espera su carta.
Day after day, she waits for his letter.

delea2/propio, propia.why: 'El pone las plumas para su propio nido' is an English idiom translated word for word into nonsense, with the pronoun él missing its accent. 'proper' is not what propio means; 'typical of' (propio de) is.
dropEx: las plumas para su propio nido
ex: Tengo mi propio coche.
I have my own car.

delea2/el alrededor.why: THE HEADWORD WAS A NOUN NOBODY USES IN THE SINGULAR. el alrededor does not stand on its own; the word is the adverb alrededor and alrededor de, 'around', which two of the three examples are, and the plural noun los alrededores, 'surroundings', which the third is. The headword becomes alrededor, with the plural noun beneath it, and 'about' for a time or a number is added. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: about, around (a time or number: alrededor de las ocho)
los alrededores — the surroundings, the outskirts
dropEx: echó una mirada alrededor de la habitación
ex: Llegaremos alrededor de las ocho.
We'll arrive at around eight.

delea2/sentirse.why: The examples and the gloss are right; the conjugation table carried both of the generator's faults. The gerund read sintíendose (S3's -iendo fault: the accent belongs on the e) and the affirmative vosotros imperative sentios (S1's: an -ir verb's i takes its accent once the d goes, sentíos).

delea2/la caja.why: 'bank' is la caja de ahorros and not the word; the sense a reader needs in a shop — la caja, the checkout — was missing. '¿Que es lo que está en la caja?' drops the accent of the question word, and the second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: checkout, till (pague en la caja — pay at the checkout)
dropEx: ¿Que es lo que está en la caja?
Estas cajas tienen mucho espacio
ex: ¿Qué hay en la caja?
What's in the box?
Pague en la caja, por favor.
Please pay at the checkout.

delea2/tranquilo, tranquila.why: 'somewhere private' is not what 'algún sitio tranquilo' says, and ¡tranquilo! — 'calm down', 'don't worry' — the everyday use, was not on the card.
exEn: Vayamos a algún sitio tranquilo
Let's go somewhere quiet where we can talk.

delea2/salvo, salva.why: THE CARD TAUGHT THE WRONG WORD. salvo as an adjective meaning 'safe' survives only in a salvo and sano y salvo; the A2 word is the preposition salvo, 'except' (todos salvo tú), which the card never mentioned. Its examples were a salvo in an A1 sentence, the verb salvar ('quien salva una vida'), and 'los niños están salvos', which is not how Spanish says it. The headword becomes salvo, its feminine and plurals go, and the two phrases stay. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: sano y salvo — safe and sound
dropEx: Este país está a salvo de un ataque.
Quien salva una vida
Los niños están salvos.
ex: Abrimos todos los días salvo los lunes.
We're open every day except Mondays.
Todos vinieron salvo Carlos.
Everyone came except Carlos.
Los niños llegaron sanos y salvos.
The children arrived safe and sound.

delea2/el hambre.why: Every example was tener hambre, one construction three times, and the card did not say what it shares with el agua: a feminine noun beginning with a stressed a- takes el in the singular — el hambre, but mucha hambre. 'las hambres' is not a plural anyone uses.
senses: morirse de hambre — to be starving
forms: feminine, but takes el in the singular: el hambre, mucha hambre
dropEx: No me puedo creer que todavía tengas hambre.
No he comido desde el desayuno
ex: El hambre es un problema en muchos países.
Hunger is a problem in many countries.
Me muero de hambre.
I'm starving.

delea2/normal.why: 'perpendicular' is a geometric sense no A2 reader needs; 'ordinary' and de lo normal, 'than usual', which the first example is, were not named. The Yanni example is a stranger's name in a stilted sentence, and the third is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: de lo normal — than usual (más tarde de lo normal)
dropEx: Los pensamientos de Yanni
Su nariz es más grande de lo normal.
ex: Es normal estar nervioso antes de un examen.
It's normal to be nervous before an exam.
Es un día normal.
It's an ordinary day.

delea2/el traje.why: 'Tu corbata hace buen par con tu traje' is not idiomatic (combina bien con), and traje de baño, 'swimsuit', which an A2 reader needs, was not named. The costume sense is already the third example.
dropEx: Tu corbata hace buen par
ex: Mi padre va a trabajar en traje.
My father goes to work in a suit.

delea2/la reunión.why: 'powwow' is not a translation and 'appointment' is la cita. 'El presidente hizo la apertura a la reunión' is stilted for abrió la reunión; the get-together sense takes its place.
dropEx: hizo la apertura a la reunión
ex: Tenemos una reunión familiar el domingo.
We have a family get-together on Sunday.

delea2/el programa.why: 'programme' and 'program' stood as two senses when they are one word spelt two ways; the computer program, which is 'program' in British English too, had no line of its own. The second example's English said 'programs' for television programmes, and the third is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: La tercera temporada del programa
exEn: en los próximos programas
There'll be quite a lot of scenes like this in the next few programmes.
ex: Este programa de ordenador no funciona.
This computer program doesn't work.

delea2/el cumpleaños.why: Two of the three examples were sentences other cards keep — la fiesta's in A1 and tal's in A2 — and ¡feliz cumpleaños!, which a reader will say first, was missing. The plural looks like the singular, which the card now says. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1). SHARED WITH AN EARLIER A2 CARD, which keeps it.
dropEx: Por favor, ven a mi fiesta de cumpleaños.
Tal vez ella se olvidó de mi cumpleaños.
ex: ¡Feliz cumpleaños!
Happy birthday!
¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños?
When is your birthday?

delea2/cualquiera.why: The card never said that before a noun the word is cualquier — any day is cualquier día — which is the form a reader meets most. 'whomever' is an archaism. The second example is the rare plural cualesquiera with an English that does not match it, and the third is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: cualquiera de los dos — either (of the two)
cualquier — any (before a noun: cualquier día)
dropEx: Eso me libera de cualesquiera
ayuda a cualquiera que se lo pida
ex: Puedes venir cualquier día.
You can come any day.
Eso lo sabe cualquiera.
Anyone knows that.

delea2/necesario, necesaria.why: 'requisite' is not a translation an A2 reader needs, and 'Favor de entregar…' is Latin American (Spain says Por favor, entreguen…). es necesario + infinitive, the construction the word lives in, had no example.
senses: es necesario + infinitive — you need to, it's necessary to
dropEx: Favor de entregar
ex: Es necesario llevar el pasaporte.
You need to bring your passport.

delea2/la sal.why: '¿Por qué no te sales de la casa?' is the verb salir, matched on shared letters; that coincidence, and the imperative sal that looks exactly like the noun, go in Forms. 'table salt' was the gloss said twice.
forms: sal — tú imperative of salir: ¡sal de aquí!
dropEx: ¿Por qué no te sales de la casa?
ex: ¿Me pasas la sal?
Could you pass me the salt?

delea2/el suelo.why: The gloss ran 'dirt, earth, ground, soil' together and gave 'ground' twice; all three examples were the floor of a house, two of them in the plural. The ground and the soil get an example each.
dropEx: Todos los suelos de su casa
Tengo que fregar los suelos.
ex: Se me cayó el móvil al suelo.
I dropped my phone on the ground.
El suelo de esta zona es muy fértil.
The soil in this area is very fertile.

delea2/el gobierno.why: Right as a card; the second translation said 'various' twice.
exEn: publica documentos secretos
This website publishes secret documents from several governments.

delea2/la cámara.why: 'room' is an archaic sense (a chamber); what the card needed was cámara de fotos, the everyday name for a camera, and the parliamentary chamber. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Ella le compró una cámara a su hijo.
ex: Siempre llevo la cámara de fotos en la mochila.
I always carry my camera in my rucksack.

delea2/la media.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES COULD STAY, AND THE GLOSS WAS TWO OTHER WORDS. 'half' is the feminine of medio (las tres y media), which has its own card; 'stocking' is las medias, which has its own card too and whose sentence this was. The first example is encima's, kept there, and the third — 'Ella gana de media 10 libras a la semana' over 'She gains on average 10 pounds a week' — is garbled beyond repair. What la media means on its own is the average. SHARED WITH AN EARLIER A2 CARD, which keeps it.
forms: medio, media — half; las medias — tights, stockings
dropEx: Mis notas están por encima de la media.
Se quitó los zapatos y las medias.
gana de media 10 libras
ex: La media de edad es de 30 años.
The average age is 30.
Duermo una media de siete horas.
I sleep an average of seven hours.
¿Cuál es la media de la clase?
What's the class average?

delea2/el regalo.why: The third example is also an A1 sentence. The other two now have Spanish names (the table gained Michael, Linda and Jenny), and the phrase for giving one had no line. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: hacer un regalo — to give a present
dropEx: trae regalos cada vez que nos visita
ex: Te he comprado un regalo.
I've bought you a present.

delea2/amable.why: 'amiable, gracious, affable' are three registers above the word; amable is the everyday 'kind', 'nice'. The third example, 'Ella invita todo el mundo', drops the personal a and its English says something else entirely. muy amable, the thanks a reader will use daily, had no line.
senses: es usted muy amable — that's very kind of you
dropEx: Ella invita todo el mundo
ex: ¿Sería tan amable de ayudarme?
Would you be so kind as to help me?

delea2/la navidad.why: THE GLOSS WAS WRONG: 'Christmas present' is un regalo de Navidad. The word is Christmas itself, written with a capital, which the headword and the first example lacked; that example's 'un día domingo' is also Latin American. ¡Feliz Navidad! and las Navidades, the season, had no line.
dropEx: Este año, la navidad cae un día domingo.
ex: ¡Feliz Navidad!
Happy Christmas!

delea2/delante.why: The gloss put 'in front of' first, which is delante de, and 'forward (with hacia preceding it)' is a note rather than a translation. 'El carro se detuvo…' uses the Latin American carro where Spain says coche.
dropEx: El carro se detuvo delante de la casa.
ex: Siéntate delante, al lado del conductor.
Sit in the front, next to the driver.

delea2/junto, junta.why: The third example is la junta, a noun meaning a board or a meeting — a different word, matched on shared letters, and now a line in Forms. The card did not say that the adjective lives in the plural, juntos, or name junto a, 'next to', which is the first example.
forms: la junta — board, meeting (a different noun)
dropEx: Voy a la junta anual
ex: Pon las sillas juntas.
Put the chairs together.

delea2/el rato.why: TWO OF THE THREE EXAMPLES WERE A RAT. 'Las ratas son el origen de la plaga' and 'una rata blanca' are la rata, matched on shared letters; only the card game was el rato. pasar un buen rato, 'to have a good time', had no line.
senses: pasar un buen rato — to have a good time
dropEx: Las ratas son el origen
comiendo una rata blanca
ex: Espérame un rato, vuelvo enseguida.
Wait for me a while, I'll be right back.
Pasamos un buen rato en la fiesta.
We had a good time at the party.

delea2/ninguno.why: The card never said that before a masculine noun the word is ningún, which is how a reader meets it most. Both of the first two examples were also A1 sentences, and the third used the plural ningunas, which is rare and not A2. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: no, not any (ningún libro, ninguna casa)
none, not one (ninguno de mis amigos)
dropEx: No he leído ninguno de los dos libros.
No conozco a ninguna de las dos muchachas.
No tomé ningunas medidas
ex: No tengo ningún problema.
I have no problem.
Ninguno de mis amigos vino.
None of my friends came.
—¿Tienes alguna pregunta? —No, ninguna.
"Have you got any questions?" "No, none."

delea2/triste.why: The gloss was a thesaurus entry ending in the Spanish word itself. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: La joven debajo del árbol se ve triste.
ex: Estoy triste porque te vas.
I'm sad because you're leaving.

delea2/el caballo, la yegua.why: The card teaches a pair and glossed only one half; 'knight' is the chess piece, not A2. montar a caballo, which the first example is, had no line.
senses: montar a caballo — to ride a horse

delea2/enseguida.why: 'Mi oficina está enseguida a la de Carlos' is not Spanish — 'next to' is al lado de — and it is where the gloss's 'next' came from. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: straight away, right away, at once
dropEx: Mi oficina está enseguida
Tengo que limpiar el cuarto de baño enseguida.
ex: Vuelvo enseguida.
I'll be right back.
Enseguida te atiendo.
I'll be with you in a moment.

delea2/agradable.why: 'agreeable' is a false friend in English, where it means willing to agree; the word is 'pleasant', 'nice'. The examples are right.

delea2/la luna.why: 'windshield' is American, and la luna for a car's window is not A2; luna de miel, 'honeymoon', is. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Había luz de luna ayer por la noche.
ex: Se fueron de luna de miel a Italia.
They went to Italy on their honeymoon.

delea2/finalmente.why: 'lastly' is a list sense no A2 reader needs, and the third example, 'salió primero un caballo que yo elegí', is stilted.
senses: finally, in the end, at last
dropEx: salió primero un caballo
ex: Finalmente, decidimos quedarnos en casa.
In the end, we decided to stay at home.

delea2/sacar.why: '(e.g. the trash)' is American and a note rather than a translation, and the gloss missed the uses its own examples show: getting something (¿de dónde has sacado…?), buying a ticket, getting a mark. The first translation said 'line' for a queue.
senses: to take out, to get out
to get (sacar entradas — to get tickets; sacar buena nota — to get a good mark)
sacar una foto — to take a photo
exEn: la cola para sacar los billetes
This is the queue for tickets.

delea2/apenas.why: 'recently, just' is Latin American usage of apenas; in Spain it means 'hardly'. The first two examples were apenas podía, one construction twice.
dropEx: apenas podía respirar
ex: Apenas hay gente en la calle.
There's hardly anyone in the street.

delea2/partido, partida.why: THE CARD TAUGHT THE WRONG WORD. It was headed as the adjective partido, 'broken', glossed in heraldic language ('per pale'), while every example was a noun: el partido, the match, which is the A2 word, and once la partida, a game of cards or chess. The headword becomes el partido, with the political party beside the match; la partida goes in Forms and its sentence makes way for the party.
forms: la partida — a game (of cards, chess)
dropEx: pierdes la partida
ex: Ana es miembro de un partido político.
Ana is a member of a political party.

delea2/el cliente, la clienta.why: The second example is also an A1 sentence, and the feminine half of the pair had no example. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Los clientes dejaron de venir
ex: La clienta pidió la cuenta.
The customer asked for the bill.

delea2/excepto.why: The first example is also an A1 sentence. excepto now shares its gloss with salvo, which S4 gave its proper sense, so the two carry a not-X hint each. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Él trabaja todos los días excepto los domingos.
ex: Me gustan todas las frutas excepto el plátano.
I like all fruit except bananas.

delea2/la espalda.why: 'backstroke' is nadar a espalda and belongs in a phrase; the third example was a shooting. a espaldas de, the second, is a real idiom and stays.
senses: a espaldas de — behind someone's back
nadar a espalda — to swim backstroke
dropEx: nos dispararon por la espalda
ex: Llevo la mochila a la espalda.
I carry my rucksack on my back.

delea2/pedir.why: The gloss had two definitions and not the sense an A2 reader uses first: to ORDER, in a restaurant. Nor did it say what separates pedir from preguntar, which is the confusion every learner has. Both of the first two examples are also A1 sentences. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to ask (someone to do something: pedir a alguien que + subjunctive)
dropEx: Vamos a pedir que nos hagan una foto.
ayuda a cualquiera que se lo pida
ex: ¿Qué vas a pedir de postre?
What are you going to order for dessert?
Le pedí ayuda a mi vecino.
I asked my neighbour for help.

delea2/el planeta.why: Right as a card; it did not say that el planeta is masculine though it ends in -a, which is the thing to learn about it.
forms: masculine, though it ends in -a: el planeta

delea2/debajo.why: Two of the three examples are also A1 sentences — and one of them is triste's too. The card now says that the word is usually debajo de. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: La joven debajo del árbol
debajo de la mesa
ex: Llevo una camiseta debajo del jersey.
I'm wearing a T-shirt under my jumper.
Mi vecina vive en el piso de debajo.
My neighbour lives in the flat below.

delea2/la estrella.why: 'Ésta estrella' puts the accent of the pronoun on a determiner, which never took one. The card did not name the star that is a famous person or a hotel rating.
senses: star (a famous person; a rating: un hotel de cuatro estrellas)
dropEx: Ésta estrella
ex: Mi hotel tiene cuatro estrellas.
My hotel has four stars.

delea2/el color.why: el color is masculine; the feminine is archaic, so 'masculine or feminine' and a plural 'los/las colores' teach a gender the reader should not use. The gloss led with the American spelling. Two examples are also A1 sentences. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: ¿de qué color es…? — what colour is…?
dropEx: El color que me encanta es el rojo.
¿De qué color es el pelo de Carlos?
ex: ¿De qué color es tu coche?
What colour is your car?
Me gustan los colores vivos.
I like bright colours.

delea2/parecer.why: 'to see fit' is a Latin American legal sense, and the card never gave the two things parecer is used for most in conversation: me parece que, 'I think', and ¿qué te parece?, 'what do you think?'. The third example makes way for the second.
senses: to seem, to look (parece cansado — he looks tired)
¿qué te parece? — what do you think?
dropEx: Las cosas no son nunca lo que parecen.
ex: ¿Qué te parece mi nuevo piso?
What do you think of my new flat?

delea2/parecerse.why: The examples are right; the gerund read parecíendose, the -iendo fault S3 found in the generator (the accent belongs on the e: pareciéndose).
senses: to look like, to resemble (parecerse a)

delea2/el/la juez.why: 'official' is not what juez means; the sports sense is 'referee', 'umpire'. The third example uses la jueza, the feminine many speakers prefer, which Forms now names.

delea2/el arte.why: 'masculine or feminine' and 'los/las artes' left a reader to guess the rule, which is that el arte is masculine in the singular and las artes feminine in the plural (las bellas artes).
forms: las artes (feminine in the plural: las bellas artes)

delea2/la obra.why: The gloss put 'work' first and every example was a play; two of the three were also A1 sentences. en obras — 'closed for works', which is how a reader in Spain meets the word most often — had no line. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: en obras — under construction, closed for works
dropEx: ¿Suele usted ir a ver obras de teatro?
¿A quién vas a traer a la obra?
ex: El Guernica es una obra de Picasso.
Guernica is a work by Picasso.
La calle está cortada por obras.
The street is closed for roadworks.

delea2/tocar.why: The second example is el toque, a noun, matched on shared letters: 'el toque de queda' is a curfew. The first is also an A1 sentence. me toca a mí, 'it's my turn', which a reader needs at every table game and every queue, had no line. The piano sentence is shared with el piano later in A2 and stays here. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to play (an instrument, a piece of music)
me toca a mí — it's my turn
le tocó la lotería — he won the lottery
dropEx: A los niños pequeños les gusta tocar todo.
toque de queda
ex: No toques eso, está caliente.
Don't touch that, it's hot.
¿A quién le toca ahora? Te toca a ti.
Whose turn is it now? It's yours.

delea2/contar.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES TAUGHT THE WORD. Two were la cuenta — 'a fin de cuentas' and 'se dio cuenta', which is darse cuenta — and the third, contar con, was also an A1 sentence. The card now shows the verb counting, telling and counted on. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: contar con — to count on, to rely on
dropEx: No deberías contar con la ayuda de otros.
A fin de cuentas
Por fin se dio cuenta
ex: Mi hijo ya sabe contar hasta cien.
My son can already count to a hundred.
¿Me cuentas qué pasó ayer?
Will you tell me what happened yesterday?
Puedes contar conmigo para la mudanza.
You can count on me for the move.

delea2/quedar.why: THE CARD TAUGHT THE OTHER VERB. All three examples were quedarse, which is the next card and shares two of them, and the first was also an A1 sentence. The gloss missed the senses quedar itself carries at A2 — to arrange to meet, to be left, to suit — and 'to be located' is ¿dónde queda?, which is a phrase. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to arrange to meet (quedar con alguien)
to be left, to remain (queda poco tiempo)
to suit, to fit (te queda bien)
dropEx: ¿Cuánto tiempo se va a quedar en Japón?
Quedarse en casa no tiene nada de divertido.
Él se quedó en casa de su tía.
ex: ¿Quedamos a las ocho en la plaza?
Shall we meet at eight in the square?
No queda leche en la nevera.
There's no milk left in the fridge.
Esa camisa te queda muy bien.
That shirt really suits you.

delea2/quedarse.why: Two of the three examples were also A1 sentences (la casa, el tío), and the same two sat on quedar. quedarse con, 'to keep, to take', and quedarse dormido had no line. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: quedarse con algo — to keep something, to take it (me quedo con este)
dropEx: Quedarse en casa no tiene nada de divertido.
Él se quedó en casa de su tía.
ex: Me quedo con la camisa azul.
I'll take the blue shirt.
Se quedó dormido en el sofá.
He fell asleep on the sofa.

delea2/probarse.why: The gloss is right. 'suéter' is the Latin American word where Spain says jersey, and the third example's Dima is not a name a Spanish sentence reaches for.
dropEx: ¿Por qué no te pruebas este suéter amarillo?
a Dima le pareció
ex: ¿Por qué no te pruebas este jersey amarillo?
Why don't you try on this yellow jumper?
Me pruebo los zapatos y nos vamos.
I'll try the shoes on and we'll go.

delea2/el vuelo.why: The gloss gave 'flight' twice over. The first example, 'Un ave levantó el vuelo en lo alto', is literary, and 'soared above' does not translate it.
dropEx: Un ave levantó el vuelo
ex: El vuelo a Londres se ha retrasado.
The flight to London has been delayed.

delea2/la nota.why: The gloss missed the school mark, which is the second example and a sense every A2 reader needs; 'grades' is American. The third example is the verb notar, matched on shared letters, and the second is shared with encima earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
senses: tomar nota — to write down, to note
dropEx: Mis notas están por encima de la media.
se le nota en la cara
ex: He sacado buena nota en el examen.
I got a good mark in the exam.
Te he dejado una nota en la nevera.
I've left you a note on the fridge.

delea2/el cuello.why: The gloss's anatomical definition is a note, and the collar of a shirt, which is how a reader buying clothes meets the word, had no line. Two of the three examples were violence: a man shot in the neck, and a robber seized by the neck in the same shape as a sentence on el brazo.
dropEx: fue herido de bala
agarró al ladrón por el cuello
exEn: cadena de oro al cuello
He put a gold chain round his neck.
ex: Me duele el cuello.
My neck hurts.
Esta camisa me aprieta el cuello.
This shirt is tight round my neck.

delea2/acaso.why: 'perhaps' is literary; acaso is met in questions that expect the answer no, and in por si acaso, 'just in case', which had no line. The second example's English dropped the word, and the third used the Latin American auto.
senses: by any chance (in a question expecting 'no': ¿acaso…?)
por si acaso — just in case
dropEx: le preguntó a Ana si acaso
¿Acaso Carlos dejó a Ana
ex: Llévate el paraguas por si acaso.
Take the umbrella just in case.
¿Acaso no lo sabías?
Didn't you know, then?

delea2/intentar.why: The gloss is right. The third example is shared with adelante earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
senses: to try (intentar + infinitive: to try to do)
dropEx: De ahora en adelante intenta llegar a tiempo.
ex: Intentamos llamarte, pero no contestabas.
We tried to ring you, but you weren't answering.

delea2/la isla.why: 'block (group of urban lots)' is a Latin American sense and not A2. The first and third examples were the same sentence with a different determiner. The first example's English said this for esa.
dropEx: La isla es un paraíso para los niños.
ex: Mallorca es la isla más grande de las Baleares.
Majorca is the largest of the Balearic Islands.
exEn: Esa isla es un paraíso
That island is a paradise for children.

delea2/la piel.why: 'pelt' is rare, and leather — un bolso de piel — is the sense a reader in a Spanish shop meets. The third example is also an A1 sentence. The wolf in sheep's clothing is shared with el cordero later in A2 and stays here. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Su piel es tan blanca como la nieve.
ex: Tengo la piel muy seca.
My skin is very dry.

delea2/el brazo.why: 'branch' and 'limb (of a tree)' are rare senses. The examples are right; the first is shared with caerse later in this batch and stays here.

delea2/recordar.why: 'recollect' and 'recall' are registers above the word, and 'remind of' did not say how the construction goes. Two of the three examples were also A1 sentences (viejo, la carta). SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: recordar algo a alguien — to remind someone of something (recuérdame que… — remind me to…)
dropEx: A ellos les gusta recordar los viejos tiempos.
Por favor recuerda echar al correo
ex: No recuerdo su nombre.
I can't remember his name.
¿Me recuerdas que compre pan?
Will you remind me to buy bread?

delea2/la visita.why: 'dar una visita al museo' is not how Spanish says it — hacer una visita — and the third example is also an A1 sentence. tener visita, 'to have visitors', had no line. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Vale la pena dar una visita al museo.
Un circo está de visita en el pueblo.
ex: La visita al museo dura una hora.
The visit to the museum lasts an hour.
Mañana tenemos visita.
We've got visitors tomorrow.

delea2/rico, rica.why: The gloss missed 'tasty', which is how a reader in Spain hears the word most — ¡qué rico! — and 'luxurious' is rare. The second and third examples were one construction.
dropEx: ¿Quién es la persona más rica de Australia?
ex: ¡Qué rica está la paella!
The paella's delicious!
exEn: seguro de que Carlos es
I'm pretty sure Carlos is rich.

delea2/pesar.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES WAS RIGHT. The first is a pesar de, a phrase built on the noun el pesar; the second is the adjective pesado, which is its own card in B1; the third weighs a brain in pounds, which a Spanish sentence does not do. The phrase stays on the card as a line.
senses: a pesar de — in spite of, despite
dropEx: A pesar de ser anciano
El oro es más pesado
El cerebro humano pesa
ex: ¿Cuánto pesas?
How much do you weigh?
La maleta pesa veinte kilos.
The suitcase weighs twenty kilos.
Tengo que pesar la harina.
I have to weigh the flour.

delea2/especialmente.why: The first and third examples were one sentence, 'Me gusta la música, especialmente…', twice.
dropEx: especialmente el rock
ex: Este año ha sido especialmente difícil.
This year has been especially difficult.

delea2/acabar.why: acabar de, 'to have just (done)', is the second example and the construction a reader meets most, and the gloss did not name it; that example's English, 'came home just now', missed it too.
senses: acabar de + infinitive — to have just (done)
exEn: acaba de llegar a casa
Carlos has just got home.

delea2/la santa.why: THE CARD TAUGHT HALF A WORD. It was headed la santa, glossed 'saintess', and two of its examples were Semana Santa, the adjective; the first said Holy Week was Easter and began on a Wednesday. The headword becomes the pair el santo, la santa, with el santo, 'saint's day', which Spain celebrates; the adjective santo is its own card in B1.
dropEx: empieza la Semana Santa
exEn: las vacaciones de Semana Santa
Where did you go for the Easter holidays?
ex: Hoy es mi santo y me han llamado mis abuelos.
Today is my saint's day and my grandparents have rung me.

delea2/la copa.why: The gloss listed five things, two of them rare (crown, treetop); the World Cup, la Copa del Mundo, had no line. The first and second examples were one construction. The first is shared with servir later in A2 and stays here.
senses: drink (tomar una copa — to have a drink)
cup (a trophy: la Copa del Mundo)
dropEx: Carlos se tomó tres copas de vino.
ex: España ganó la Copa del Mundo en 2010.
Spain won the World Cup in 2010.

delea2/cansado, cansada.why: 'wearied' is not English a reader would use, and 'boring' is not what the word means: ser cansado is 'tiring'. The first and third examples were one construction.
dropEx: Estamos tan cansados que no somos capaces
ex: El viaje fue muy cansado.
The journey was very tiring.

delea2/subir.why: The gloss missed getting on a bus or a train, and turning something up; the examples are right, and the third is shared with la bicicleta later in A2 and stays here.
senses: to go up, to come up (subir la escalera)
to get on (a bus, a train: subir al autobús)
to raise, to turn up (subir el volumen)

delea2/preocupado, preocupada.why: 'De eso es de lo que estoy preocupado' is not Spanish — worry about something is preocupado por — and the second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: De eso es de lo que estoy preocupado.
Ella estaba preocupada por la salud de él.
ex: Estoy preocupado por el examen.
I'm worried about the exam.
¿Por qué estás tan preocupada?
Why are you so worried?

delea2/caerse.why: THE CONJUGATION TABLE CARRIED TWO GENERATOR FAULTS. The gerund read cayendose (S3's fault: -yendo was missed, cayéndose), and the affirmative usted and ustedes imperatives read caígase and caíganse, the accent on the i of a diphthong where Spanish writes cáigase and cáiganse — a new fault, corrected in build_deck.py, which counted the stress in vowels rather than syllables. Of the examples, the first is shared with el brazo earlier in this batch, and the third, 'La lluvia no se cae del suelo', is nonsense. se me ha caído, 'I've dropped it', had no line.
senses: se me ha caído — I've dropped it
dropEx: Carlos se cayó y se rompió el brazo.
La lluvia no se cae del suelo.
ex: Se me ha caído el móvil.
I've dropped my phone.
Cuidado, que te caes.
Careful, you'll fall.

delea2/la red.why: 'web' and 'mesh' are not how the word is met; a network — una red social, la red wifi — is, and had no line. The card also carried two examples where the type shows three. The first is shared with social later in A2 and stays here.
senses: network (una red social; la red — the internet)
ex: No encuentro la red wifi del hotel.
I can't find the hotel's wifi network.

delea2/solamente.why: 'alone' is solo, the adjective, and not this word; 'merely' is a register above it. The examples are right.

delea2/el ruido.why: The gloss was a thesaurus entry ending in a sense from electronics. The first and third examples were one construction, No hagas… ruido, and the first's English dropped its article.
exEn: El bebé está durmiendo
The baby's asleep. Don't make so much noise.
dropEx: No hagas ni un ruido
ex: Hay mucho ruido en esta calle.
There's a lot of noise in this street.

delea2/el gato, la gata.why: 'tomcat' and 'gib' are not the word; the card teaches the pair, and the gloss did not say what the feminine is. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: A los gatos no les gusta el agua.
ex: Mi gata ha tenido cuatro gatitos.
My cat has had four kittens.

delea2/la pasada.why: TWO OF THE THREE EXAMPLES WERE THE ADJECTIVE pasada, which is the card pasado, pasada earlier in A2: 'pasada de moda' and 'las pasadas dos horas'. The gloss — transit, crossing, moment — describes none of them. What the noun is at A2 is the colloquial ¡qué pasada!, which the third example is, and dar una pasada, a quick wipe or going-over; 'awesome' is American.
senses: a quick going-over, a wipe (dar una pasada a algo)
dropEx: un poco pasada de moda
en las pasadas dos horas
exEn: la película era una pasada
I thought the film was amazing.
ex: Dale una pasada a la mesa con un trapo.
Give the table a wipe with a cloth.
¡Qué pasada de concierto!
What an amazing concert!

delea2/alguno.why: The card never said that before a masculine noun the word is algún, which is how a reader meets it most, and it named no pronoun use. Two of the three examples were also A1 sentences. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: si es que hay alguno
Algunas veces no puedo evitar
ex: ¿Tienes algún libro de cocina?
Have you got a cookery book?
Alguno de vosotros tendrá un bolígrafo.
One of you must have a pen.

delea2/el hielo.why: The gloss is right. The second example, ice sheets translated as 'permafrost', is not A2 and is not what permafrost is; ice in a drink is. The third is shared with el deporte later in A2 and stays here.
dropEx: cubierta por hielos perpetuos
ex: ¿Me pones un refresco con hielo?
Could I have a soft drink with ice?

delea2/coger.why: The gloss was a list of five near-synonyms and 'harvest'. The first example is also an A1 sentence, and the card did not warn that in much of Latin America coger is vulgar, where tomar or agarrar is used instead. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to take (coger el autobús — to catch the bus)
to pick up, to take hold of
forms: in much of Latin America coger is vulgar; tomar or agarrar is used instead
dropEx: Voy a coger el tren de las once.
exEn: coge todo lo que te guste
Please take whatever you like.
ex: Coge el paraguas, que va a llover.
Take the umbrella, it's going to rain.

delea2/seguramente.why: The word means 'probably', not 'surely': seguramente lloverá is a forecast, not a certainty, and the examples' English said 'surely' twice. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Seguramente él me llamará por teléfono
exEn: habría hecho lo mismo por ti
Carlos would probably have done the same for you.
está cansada después de una larga marcha
