She's probably tired after a long walk.
ex: Seguramente lloverá mañana.
It will probably rain tomorrow.

delea2/la pared.why: The second example wrote los paredes: the word is feminine, las paredes. The third is also an A1 sentence. The first is shared with el cuadro later in A2 and stays here. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: wall (of a room, of a building)
dropEx: No puedo ver a través de los paredes.
Mirad con atención el mapa de la pared.
ex: Vamos a pintar las paredes de blanco.
We're going to paint the walls white.
Las paredes de este piso son muy finas.
The walls in this flat are very thin.

delea2/la naturaleza.why: The gloss did not separate the natural world from a person's nature, and the second example, about men confronting their 'sensitive inner natures', is neither A2 nor natural. The third is shared with político later in A2 and stays here.
dropEx: No son lo bastante hombres
ex: Me encanta pasear por la naturaleza.
I love walking in the countryside.

delea2/arreglar.why: The gloss ran nine English verbs together and missed tidying a room. The first example's English turned a causative (llevar a arreglar) into 'get repaired by tomorrow'; the third used the Latin American auto.
senses: to fix, to repair, to mend
dropEx: tu auto alguna vez
exEn: Llevaré a arreglar estos zapatos
I'll take these shoes to be mended before tomorrow.
ex: Ya he arreglado el ordenador.
I've already fixed the computer.

delea2/sentado, sentada.why: 'el puesto del frente' is not how Spanish says the front seat, and 'una bomba de tiempo' is Latin American (Spain: de relojería). The second example is right.
dropEx: en el puesto del frente
sobre una bomba de tiempo
ex: Estaba sentada en el sofá viendo la tele.
She was sitting on the sofa watching TV.
Los niños están sentados a la mesa.
The children are sitting at the table.

delea2/la política.why: The gloss is right apart from a definition standing in for a translation. The first example's English read saben as 'you know' where it is 'they know'.
exEn: Saben que la política
They know nothing good comes of politics.

delea2/la enfermedad.why: The gloss and the examples are right; the third example's English said 'most diseases' for muchas, 'many'. The first is shared with la medicina later in A2 and stays here.
exEn: Como muchas enfermedades
Like many diseases, it has its own symptoms.

delea2/el príncipe.why: 'sovereign' and 'ruler' are archaic senses. The third example, 'Prince Charles will be the next British king', stopped being true in 2022.
dropEx: El príncipe Carlos será
ex: El príncipe se casó con una periodista.
The prince married a journalist.

delea2/bajar.why: TWO OF THE THREE EXAMPLES WERE THE ADJECTIVE bajo, baja: 'la temperatura más baja' and 'un poco bajo para mí'. The gloss missed turning something down, prices falling and downloading.
senses: to go down, to come down
to get off (a bus, a train)
to lower, to turn down (bajar el volumen)
to fall, to come down (prices, temperatures)
bajar(se) una canción — to download a song
dropEx: La temperatura más baja de hoy
un poco bajo para mí
ex: Baja la música, por favor.
Turn the music down, please.
Los precios han bajado este mes.
Prices have come down this month.

delea2/nervioso, nerviosa.why: 'nerve' is a noun, el nervio, and not this word; nervioso also names what belongs to the nerves, el sistema nervioso. The examples are right.
senses: nervous (of the nerves: el sistema nervioso)

delea2/la emergencia.why: 'emergence' is not this word. The first and third examples were the same sentence with a comma, and the second's sala de emergencias is Latin American, where Spain says urgencias.
forms: a hospital's A&E is urgencias in Spain
dropEx: Carlos terminó en la sala de emergencias.
En caso de emergencia, llama a la policía.
ex: Es una emergencia, ¿puede venir un médico?
It's an emergency: can a doctor come?
Esta es la salida de emergencia.
This is the emergency exit.

delea2/la botella.why: 'tank' is not this word (a gas bottle is una bombona). The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Las botellas de cerveza están hechas de vidrio.
ex: Una botella de agua, por favor.
A bottle of water, please.

delea2/la distancia.why: The third example, 'La distancia fue más grande que yo esperé', is not Spanish (the tense is esperaba) and its English said 'gap'. The first is shared with la llamada earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: una llamada a larga distancia
más grande que yo esperé
ex: ¿Qué distancia hay de Madrid a Toledo?
How far is it from Madrid to Toledo?
Vivimos a poca distancia del colegio.
We live a short distance from the school.

delea2/la pierna.why: The gloss is a definition, and it did not say that an animal's or a table's leg is la pata. The second example is also an A1 sentence, and the first and third were one construction, se hizo… en la pierna. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
forms: la pata — leg of an animal, of a table
dropEx: Mis piernas son más pequeñas
Carlos se ha hecho daño en la pierna.
ex: Me duele la pierna izquierda.
My left leg hurts.
Cruzó las piernas y empezó a leer.
She crossed her legs and started to read.

delea2/el/la ex.why: The gloss split one sense over two bullets. The third example called someone a psychopath, which a vocabulary card has no call to teach.
dropEx: tu ex es una psicópata
ex: Mi ex y yo seguimos siendo amigos.
My ex and I are still friends.

delea2/recibir.why: The gloss is right bar its layout. The first example's English, 'We're about to have guests', dropped the verb; it is shared with invitar later in A2 and stays here.
exEn: a punto de recibir a los invitados
We're about to welcome the guests.

delea2/cerdo, cerda.why: THE CARD TAUGHT THE WRONG WORD. It was headed as the adjective, glossed 'dirty', a colloquial insult, while every example was the noun: pork, pigs, a sow. The headword becomes the pair el cerdo, la cerda, with pork; the insult goes in a line. The third example, a sow raffled in a square, is not a sentence a reader will need. The first is shared with la vaca later in A2 and stays here.
dropEx: En la plaza sortean una cerda.
ex: En la granja tienen gallinas y cerdos.
They have hens and pigs on the farm.

delea2/contento, contenta.why: The gloss is right. The first example's English, 'I am contented with my lot', is two registers above the Spanish.
exEn: con mi situación en la vida
I'm happy with my situation in life.

delea2/romper.why: The gloss named 'to break up' without the construction, romper con alguien. The first and third examples both broke the window, the first in a stilted cleft. The second is shared with la compra later in A2 and stays here.
senses: romper con alguien — to break up with someone
dropEx: Lo que ellos hicieron fue romper
ex: Ana ha roto con su novio.
Ana has broken up with her boyfriend.

delea2/la medicina.why: The gloss did not separate a medicine from medicine the subject. The first example is shared with la enfermedad earlier in A2; the second's English said 'medications'. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: La medicina es el estudio de las enfermedades.
exEn: las medicinas que necesites
Write down the medicines you need on this piece of paper.
ex: Mi hermana estudia Medicina en Salamanca.
My sister is studying medicine in Salamanca.

delea2/el pollo.why: THE THIRD EXAMPLE WAS SEXUALLY EXPLICIT and not about this word at all: 'prefiero las pollas de verdad' is la polla, a vulgar word for the penis, matched on shared letters, with a translation to match. A sweep of every example in the seven Spanish decks for vulgar vocabulary (with Unicode-aware word boundaries) found no other. The second example kept six chickens as pets, which are gallinas; the first's 'hoy a la noche' is Rioplatense for esta noche.
dropEx: prefiero las pollas de verdad
seis pollos
cocinar pollo hoy a la noche
ex: Hoy comemos pollo asado.
We're having roast chicken today.
Me gustaría cocinar pollo esta noche.
I'd like to cook chicken tonight.
El pollo ya está en el horno.
The chicken's already in the oven.

delea2/varios.why: The gloss is right. The second example's English said 'many times' for varias veces.
exEn: ver esta película varias veces
This film is worth seeing several times.

delea2/el sombrero.why: 'butterfly pea (Clitorea ternatea)' is a plant and nothing a reader will meet. The examples are right.

delea2/menor.why: THE GLOSS GAVE ONLY THE LEGAL SENSE, 'underage', while two of the three examples were 'younger' and 'youngest', which is how the word is met at A2. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: menor de edad — a minor, under age
dropEx: Esa es la fotografía de mi hermana menor.
ex: Mi hermano es dos años menor que yo.
My brother is two years younger than me.

delea2/limpio, limpia.why: The third example is the verb limpiar ('¿por qué limpias la casa?'), matched on shared letters.
dropEx: limpias la casa todas las semanas
ex: La ropa limpia está en el armario.
The clean clothes are in the wardrobe.

delea2/la china.why: THE CARD WAS HEADED AS THE WRONG WORD. la china is a pebble, which is what it was glossed as, and every example was China, the country. The country is what an A2 reader needs; the pebble goes in Forms, and the nationality, chino, china, is its own card later in A2. Two of the three examples were also one sentence (a book written about China, a book written in China), and the first is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Él ha escrito un libro acerca de China.
Él escribió un libro cuando estaba en China.
ex: Mi hermana vive en China desde hace dos años.
My sister has been living in China for two years.
La Gran Muralla está en el norte de China.
The Great Wall is in the north of China.

delea2/el dedo.why: 'digit' is not how English names a finger, and toes, dedos del pie, had no line. The examples are right.

delea2/elegir.why: The gloss is right. The second example, about a horse the speaker picked coming first, is the sentence S5 took off finalmente, where it was also stilted.
dropEx: salió primero un caballo que yo elegí
ex: Elige el postre que quieras.
Choose whatever dessert you like.

delea2/la costa.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES WAS THE COAST. All three were a toda costa or a costa de, 'at any cost', which is costa in the sense of cost, built on costar. The phrase stays on the card as a line.
senses: a toda costa — at all costs
dropEx: irse a casa a toda costa
a costas de su vida propia
defender nuestro país a toda costa
ex: Pasamos el verano en la costa.
We spent the summer on the coast.
Málaga está en la costa del sur de España.
Málaga is on the south coast of Spain.
Esta ciudad está a cien kilómetros de la costa.
This town is a hundred kilometres from the coast.

delea2/el cuento.why: All three examples were fairy tales, and the third's English said 'fairy tales' for plain cuentos. The second is shared with la princesa earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: Ana es una princesa de cuento de hadas.
exEn: les encanta escuchar cuentos
Children love listening to stories.
ex: Mi abuela me contaba cuentos antes de dormir.
My grandmother used to tell me stories at bedtime.

delea2/enviar.why: The gloss is right. The first example's 'mañana en la mañana' is Latin American, where Spain says mañana por la mañana, and its English said 'mail'.
dropEx: mañana en la mañana
ex: Te envío las fotos por correo electrónico.
I'll send you the photos by email.

delea2/impresionante.why: 'awesome' is American. The third example, 'Ese vestido se ve impresionante en ti', is a calque of the English 'looks good on you', where Spanish says te queda.
dropEx: Ese vestido se ve impresionante en ti.
ex: Las vistas desde la torre son impresionantes.
The views from the tower are amazing.

delea2/explicar.why: 'to explain oneself' is explicarse, and ¿me explico? had no line. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: ¿me explico? — do you see what I mean?
dropEx: La semana que viene lo explicaré en detalle.
ex: ¿Me puedes explicar cómo funciona esto?
Can you explain how this works?

delea2/el alcohol.why: 'galena' is a mineral and not this word. The first example is also an A1 sentence, and in the third el cigarro is a cigar in Spain where the English read 'smoking'. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: no tengo ganas de beber alcohol
dejó el cigarro y el alcohol
exEn: Mi padre ha dejado de beber alcohol
My father has given up alcohol.
ex: Esta cerveza no tiene alcohol.
This beer has no alcohol in it.
Él dejó el tabaco y el alcohol.
He gave up smoking and drinking.

delea2/antiguo, antigua.why: The gloss was a thesaurus ('erstwhile, quondam, onetime'), and it did not say that before a noun the word means 'former': mi antiguo jefe. The first example is also an A1 sentence, set in Boston; the third's English made two ruins one. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: former (before the noun: mi antiguo jefe)
dropEx: el restaurante más antiguo de Boston
exEn: Esas antiguas ruinas
Those ancient ruins were once a temple.
ex: Mi antiguo jefe vive ahora en Sevilla.
My former boss now lives in Seville.

delea2/el queso.why: The gloss is right. The third example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: El queso se hace a partir de leche.
ex: Un bocadillo de queso, por favor.
A cheese sandwich, please.

delea2/olvidar.why: The gloss did not say that the verb is usually olvidarse de, which two of its examples are. The second is shared with tal earlier in A2. The third is shared with acordarse later in A2 and stays here. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
senses: to forget (olvidar algo, olvidarse de algo)
to leave behind (he olvidado el paraguas)
dropEx: Tal vez ella se olvidó de mi cumpleaños.
ex: He olvidado las llaves en casa.
I've left my keys at home.

delea2/el techo.why: The gloss is right, though a pitched roof in Spain is el tejado. The second example, that Japan's ceilings are low for foreigners, is a claim rather than a sentence; the first's English said 'in behalf of', the third's 'our building' for nuestra casa.
dropEx: Los techos de Japón
exEn: habló en favor de los sin techo
She spoke on behalf of the homeless.
voló el techo de nuestra casa
The wind blew the roof off our house.
ex: Esta habitación tiene el techo muy alto.
This room has a very high ceiling.

delea2/el bote.why: The gloss ran ten words together. The card missed that in Spain el bote is at least as often a jar or a tin, and the first example, de bote en bote, is also an A1 sentence. The phrase stays on the card as a line. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: jar, tin, can (un bote de tomate)
de bote en bote — packed, full to bursting
dropEx: La sala estaba llena de bote en bote.
ex: Compra un bote de tomate frito.
Buy a jar of tomato sauce.

delea2/la rosa.why: 'pink' is rosa the colour, which is an adjective and invariable (unos zapatos rosa). The examples are right.

delea2/compartir.why: The gloss is right bar a gloss-within-a-gloss. The second example's English said 'apartment'.
exEn: Todos en el apartamento compartimos la cocina
Everyone in the flat shares the kitchen.

delea2/la esquina.why: The first and third examples were one sentence, 'vive a la vuelta de la esquina'.
dropEx: Carlos vive a la vuelta de la esquina.
ex: Gira a la derecha en la próxima esquina.
Turn right at the next corner.

delea2/la tormenta.why: The first example said the power went off 'gracias a la tormenta', thanks to it, where Spanish says por. The third's English, 'a tempest in a teapot', is American; British English says 'a storm in a teacup'.
dropEx: Se cortó la luz gracias a la tormenta.
exEn: una tormenta en un vaso de agua
It's a storm in a teacup.
ex: Anoche hubo una tormenta muy fuerte.
There was a very heavy storm last night.

delea2/la ciencia.why: 'erudition' and 'knowledge' are old senses. The second example, 'Ese profesor de ciencias maneja todos los años', is nonsense in Spain, where manejar is not 'to drive', and its English says nothing either.
dropEx: maneja todos los años
exEn: no le gusta la ciencia ficción
Ana doesn't like science fiction.
ex: Mi asignatura favorita es Ciencias Naturales.
My favourite subject is natural science.

delea2/sucio, sucia.why: 'sinful' and 'tainted' are figurative senses nobody at A2 needs. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Los bancos del parque están sucios y rotos.
ex: Pon la ropa sucia en la lavadora.
Put the dirty clothes in the washing machine.

delea2/la bebida.why: The third example, 'He comido la comida y bebido la bebida', teaches nothing and its English said 'drank' for the participle; the second, 'los demás tipos de bebidas', is stilted.
dropEx: He comido la comida y bebido la bebida.
los demás tipos de bebidas
ex: ¿Qué bebidas tienen?
What drinks have you got?
La comida y la bebida están incluidas en el precio.
Food and drink are included in the price.

delea2/la lluvia.why: The gloss is right. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Las plantas crecen rápidamente después de la lluvia.
ex: Mañana se espera lluvia en el norte.
Rain is expected in the north tomorrow.

delea2/el curso.why: The gloss ran a course of a river, a trajectory and a class together, and missed the school year, el curso escolar, which is how the word is met most. The first example is also an A1 sentence; the third's English said 'class' for a year group. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Este martes, los alumnos han comenzado el curso.
exEn: el más alto de nuestro curso
Carlos is the tallest in our year.
ex: El curso empieza en septiembre.
The school year starts in September.

delea2/probable.why: 'provable' is not this word. The second example, a weather forecast with 'probables precipitaciones', is the language of the bulletin, not A2.
senses: es probable que + subjunctive — it's likely that…
lo más probable es que… — most likely…
dropEx: con probables precipitaciones
exEn: Es muy probable que Carlos sepa
It's very likely that Carlos knows the truth.
ex: Lo más probable es que lleguemos tarde.
We'll most likely be late.

delea2/parecido, parecida.why: The first example is the verb parecer ('¿Qué les ha parecido su viaje?'), matched on shared letters, and is shared with el viaje earlier in A2. The noun el parecido, 'likeness', had no line. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: ¿Qué les ha parecido su viaje a Australia?
ex: Tenemos gustos muy parecidos.
We have very similar tastes.

delea2/efectivo, efectiva.why: The gloss put 'real, true' first and missed the noun its own first example is: en efectivo, 'in cash', which a reader uses at every till. The second example was about missiles; the third's English said 'the medicine used proved' for solía ser.
dropEx: Esos misiles son cien por ciento
exEn: Esta medicina solía ser muy efectiva
This medicine used to be very effective.
ex: ¿Aceptan tarjeta o solo efectivo?
Do you take cards or only cash?

delea2/el/la artista.why: The gloss ran four near-synonyms together. The examples are right; the third is shared with el dibujo later in A2 and stays here.

delea2/la entrevista.why: The gloss is right. The second example, 'Trata de mirar algunas entrevistas recientes', is a calque of 'try to look at'.
dropEx: Trata de mirar algunas entrevistas recientes.
ex: Le hicieron una entrevista en la radio.
They interviewed him on the radio.

delea2/helado, helada.why: THE CARD TAUGHT THE WRONG WORD. It was headed as the adjective, glossed 'icy, frozen, shocked', while two of the three examples were el helado, ice cream, which is the A2 word. The headword becomes the noun and the adjective goes in Forms. The second example, 'No hay nada como el verano y helados', is not a sentence; the third was the adjective.
forms: helado, helada (adjective) — frozen, freezing: el agua está helada
dropEx: No hay nada como el verano y helados.
despertar en las mañanas heladas
ex: ¿De qué sabor quieres el helado?
What flavour ice cream do you want?
Un helado de chocolate, por favor.
A chocolate ice cream, please.

delea2/el rock.why: The word has no plural in use, and the card gave one ('los rocks'). The first example is shared with perder earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: Pablo perdió su interés en la música rock.
exEn: el rey del rock
He was the king of rock and roll.
ex: Me gusta el rock de los años ochenta.
I like eighties rock.

delea2/responder.why: 'to talk back' and 'to answer back' are contestar, which is A1's card. The first example's Tommy is not a Spanish name, and the second is also an A1 sentence. The third is shared with chino later in A2 and stays here. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to answer, to reply (responder a algo)
dropEx: Tommy no pudo responder
Carlos no respondió a la pregunta de Ana.
ex: No me has respondido al mensaje.
You haven't replied to my message.
Llamé tres veces, pero nadie respondió.
I rang three times, but nobody answered.

delea1.why: THE DECK HAD NO THIRD-PERSON OBJECT PRONOUN AT ALL. supplement.py's PRONOUNS list names me, te, se, nos and os and stops, so DELE A1 shipped with cards for los and unas and nothing for lo, la, le or les - the pronouns an A1 reader needs the moment they stop using a noun twice in a sentence. The only trace of them was the los card's gloss, which called it 'a plural masculine or neuter pronoun' and gave no English at all; that card is now folded into the definite article, so without this the sense would have gone entirely. It also carries the neuter article lo, which turns an adjective into a noun (lo importante) and is a construction with no other home in the deck. The paradigm goes in Forms rather than in the headword, so the front of the card is not one letter away from the article's. Its Forms rows are the pronoun's own paradigm and not words to mark up, so the card names what may be bolded: deriving from them would bold the ARTICLE la in 'lo importante es la salud'.
senses: the … thing, what is … (neuter, before an adjective: lo importante)
ex: No lo sé.
I don't know.
Lo compré ayer.
I bought it yesterday.
Lo importante es la salud.
The important thing is health.

delea1.why: The indirect object, missing for the same reason as lo. It carries the se rule in Forms - le and les become se before lo, la, los and las - which is the one thing about Spanish pronouns a reader cannot guess, and which the deck already shows in an example on the por card ('¿Por qué no se lo dijiste a ella?') without ever explaining. les is a form rather than a card, on the same reasoning that folded el, la, los and las into one.
senses: to him, to her, to you (formal) — indirect object
ex: Le di el libro a María.
I gave the book to María.
¿Qué le pasa?
What's the matter with him?
Les escribí una carta.
I wrote them a letter.

delea1.why: cómo had a card and como, one accent away and just as common, had none - so the deck taught the question word and not the ordinary conjunction that means 'as' or 'like'. It is also the one that turns up in a comparison (tan alto como) and in a reason clause (como llueve, no salgo), neither of which the deck could say anywhere. It is also the first person of comer, which is why the comer card's own examples bold it.
forms: with an accent, the question word
ex: Es tan alto como su padre.
He's as tall as his father.
Trabaja como profesor.
He works as a teacher.
Como llueve, no salgo.
Since it's raining, I'm not going out.

delea1.why: esto and eso each had a card and aquello, the third of the same set of three, had none - so the deck taught two thirds of a closed class and left the reader to guess the rest.
senses: that (neuter, further off — an idea, a situation, or something not yet named)
ex: Aquello fue muy difícil.
That was very difficult.
No me gustó nada aquello.
I didn't like that at all.
¿Te acuerdas de aquello?
Do you remember that?

delea1.why: The same gap as como, one accent over. supplement.py's QUESTION list names the ACCENTED interrogatives - qué, quién, cómo, cuándo, dónde, cuánto - and the deck therefore taught six question words and not one of the ordinary conjunctions written the same way without the accent. cuando is among the commonest words in Spanish and had no card. (donde is added beside it; quien and cual are deliberately left out — the relative quien is a B1 word and el cual is further on still, so adding them here would be teaching above the level rather than filling a gap.)
forms: with an accent, the question word
ex: Te llamo cuando llegue.
I'll call you when I arrive.
Cuando era niño, vivía en Madrid.
When I was a child, I lived in Madrid.
Ven cuando quieras.
Come whenever you like.

delea1.why: See the cuando entry: the unaccented half of a question word the deck taught only as a question.
senses: where (as a relative: la casa donde vivo — the house where I live)
forms: with an accent, the question word
ex: Esta es la casa donde vivo.
This is the house where I live.
Vamos donde tú quieras.
Let's go wherever you like.
El pueblo donde nació es muy pequeño.
The village where he was born is very small.
